subject: Acceptance criteria for third-party security assessment reports and vendor qualifications
messages:
From: Tim McLeod <security@acme-corp.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Question on acceptance window for third-party assessment reports

Hi Olga / Lauren,

We're in the final stages of our vendor review for Redwood. The security team reviewed the SOC 2 materials — thanks — and we have one outstanding item from procurement: acceptance of previously completed penetration test reports.

Specifically: our policy allows a third-party pen test report to be accepted for vendor onboarding if the engagement concluded within the last 12 months and the vendor uses an accredited firm that follows OWASP/OSSTMM or similar modern methodologies. Acme's security officer wants to confirm Redwood's position on: 

- Whether Redwood accepts a 2025-11-20 pen test report (attached) for current onboarding or if a fresh assessment is required.
- What firm validation you perform (e.g., firm creds, certifications, sample report redaction review).
- Whether Redwood can provide a short checklist we can attach to our procurement file confirming scope, methodology, and remediation status.

Can you confirm? We're trying to avoid an extra test if possible, but procurement will escalate if we don't have a clear acceptance path.

Thanks,
Tim
Security Manager — Acme Industries
attachments: Redwood-PT-Report-2025-11-20.pdf

From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Tim McLeod <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Question on acceptance window for third-party assessment reports

Tim —

Thanks for the clear note and for sharing the report. Short answer up front: we generally accept recent third-party reports (<=12 months) conditionally — acceptance depends on (1) firm credentials, (2) methodology alignment, (3) whether critical/high findings are remediated and verified, and (4) whether the scope covers production-facing inference endpoints and admin consoles.

I'll summarize what we can provide to help procurement: a short one-page "Assessment Acceptance Checklist" that calls out firm name, engagement dates, methodology, critical findings & remediation status, and whether the scope includes externally exposed services. I've attached a template (Redwood-PT-Checklist.xlsx) which you can attach to your file.

Next steps I propose:
- We'll ask our vendor (BlackHat Security) to provide a short engagement summary and a methodology statement.
- We will indicate whether findings classified as critical/high were remediated and verified (we require verification for all critical/high).
- If verification was not performed after the 2025-11-20 engagement, we will either schedule a focused retest or provide compensating controls and a remediation plan with timelines.

Lauren / Markus — looped in for visibility. Markus, can you confirm the minimum vendor qualifications we require (certs, sample report availability) and whether we will accept OSSTMM/OWASP-based methodology claims without additional evidence?

Olga
Senior Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood-PT-Checklist.xlsx

From: Priya Shah <engagements@blackhatsec.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim McLeod <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 14:25:00 -0500
Subject: BlackHat Security — engagement summary and methodology for Acme report

Hi Olga / Lauren —

Thanks for the request. Attached is an engagement summary for the 2025-11-20 assessment we delivered for Redwood's environment for Acme (BlackHatSec-Engagement-Summary.pdf). To address your specific questions: 

- Firm credentials: BlackHat Security is CHECK-registered and holds CREST membership; engagement leads hold OSCP/OSCE and CREST Practitioner certifications.
- Methodology: the engagement combined automated scanning (credentialed and unauthenticated) with manual verification and business-logic testing. Coverage map included in the summary — key in-scope assets were production inference API, model hosting nodes, admin SSO, and CI/CD pipelines used for model deploys. We reference OWASP ASVS and selective OSSTMM controls depending on the asset class.
- Findings & remediation: The final report (Redwood-PT-Report-2025-11-20.pdf) included two high-risk findings and five medium findings. Both high-risk items were fixed in late Dec 2025 and BlackHatSec performed verification checks in Jan 2026; evidence of verification (screenshots, retest notes) is included in the engagement summary appendix.

If Acme's procurement requires a retest window of less than 12 months, note that our verification work extends the acceptance window effectively to the date of verification (Jan 2026). We can provide a short attestation letter if that helps.

Let us know if you'd like a brief phone call to walk through methodology and artifacts; happy to schedule.

Best,
Priya Shah
Engagement Director — BlackHat Security
attachments: BlackHatSec-Engagement-Summary.pdf

From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Tim McLeod <security@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <engagements@blackhatsec.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Acceptance criteria for third-party security assessment reports and vendor qualifications

Tim —

Following up after Priya's note: based on the vendor attestation and the verification performed in Jan 2026, Redwood is comfortable confirming the attached 2025-11-20 assessment as acceptable for procurement purposes. Key points we will record on your checklist: 

- Firm: BlackHat Security (CREST member, CHECK-registered).
- Engagement date: 2025-11-20 (report); verification performed Jan 2026.
- Methodology: mixed automated/manual testing referencing OWASP/OSSTMM/ASVS controls.
- Findings: 2 high (both remediated and verified), 5 medium (remediated).
- Scope: production inference endpoints, admin SSO, model hosting. 

Attached is a filled version of the Redwood-PT-Checklist.xlsx for your procurement file and a short attestation text you can paste into your vendor acceptance form. If procurement needs an explicit signed attestation, Priya has offered to provide one.

If procurement still requires a fresh, dedicated pen test regardless of verification (we've seen this in some regulated buyers), please let us know and we can provide cost/time estimates for a targeted retest covering the verified high findings only.

Thanks — glad we could avoid an extra engagement on this one.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood-PT-Checklist.xlsx, attestation-text.txt
